# Amy Comer Succeeds Jill Albertelli as President of Pratt & Whitney Military Engines


October 01, 2026


- Share this article on Facebook
- Share this article on Twitter
- Share this article on LinkedIn
- Share this article via email


EAST HARTFORD, Conn., Oct. 1, 2026 – Pratt & Whitney today named Amy Comer president of its Military Engines business, effective Jan. 1, 2027. Comer succeeds Jill Albertelli, who was recently appointed Pratt & Whitney president, upon Shane Eddy’s retirement at the end of the year. Pratt & Whitney is an RTX business (NYSE: RTX).


“Amy is a trusted leader with deep technical expertise and a proven track record of disciplined execution for our customers,” said Eddy. “I’m confident she will build on Jill’s significant efforts and ensure we continue to deliver the advanced propulsion capabilities the U.S. Services and our allies need for their important missions.”


Comer brings more than 20 years of experience to this role in leadership positions across engineering and program management, supporting the development and sustainment of military and commercial product lines. She is currently vice president of Pratt & Whitney’s GTF engines.


**About RTX**
With more than 180,000 global employees, we push the limits of technology and science to redefine how we connect and protect our world. With industry-leading capabilities, we advance aviation, engineer integrated defense systems for operational success, and develop next-generation technology solutions and manufacturing to help global customers address their most critical challenges. The company, with 2025 sales of more than $88 billion, is headquartered in Arlington, Virginia.
